detailed_description: The Regex Visualizer transforms regular expressions into interactive railroad diagrams by parsing pattern syntax into directed graph structures. This tool leverages finite automaton theory to map capture groups, quantifiers, and alternations into visual components, displaying regex logic as interconnected nodes and edges. Developers benefit from concrete visualization of abstract pattern logic, particularly useful for debugging complex expressions with nested lookaheads or balancing groups. The tool supports multiple regex engines (PCRE, Python, JavaScript) and includes real-time matching analysis against test strings, highlighting capture group boundaries and failure points. Built with a WebAssembly-powered regex parser, it provides instant feedback without server-side processing, ensuring sensitive patterns remain client-local.
usage_steps: Input regex pattern in the syntax-highlighted editor, with dropdown selection for target engine (PCRE/Python/JS)
Toggle 'Debug View' to display state transitions in the automaton diagram
Enter test strings in the parallel input panel to see match visualizations with colored path tracing
Click specific nodes in the diagram to highlight corresponding regex tokens and capture groups
Adjust quantifier bounds using interactive sliders to experiment with pattern variations
Export SVG diagram or copy analysis report with match details and engine compatibility notes
usage_examples: Validating email address patterns by visualizing RFC 5322-compliant regex structure
Optimizing log parsing expressions through visual identification of backtracking hotspots
Teaching regex syntax to junior developers using interactive diagram annotations
Reverse-engineering complex validation patterns from legacy codebases through visual decomposition
